name: USD.AI
oneLiner: USDai is USD.AI's non-yielding base dollar, backed 1:1 by PYUSD and separately stakeable into sUSDai for GPU-loan yield.

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from Pharos stablecoin metadata by the blacklistability resolver through parent, reserve, custody, variant, or text-signal exposure; no separate manual override source is attached.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Inferred review retained: USDai resolves to Upstream because existing dependency, reserve, custody, variant, or text metadata links exposure to a freezable upstream asset.

collateral: PYUSD held by the canonical USDai contract on Arbitrum and reconciled 1:1 against canonical plus bridged USDai liabilities; GPU-loan DEAL exposure belongs to the separate sUSDai yield layer
pegMechanism: Users mint and redeem canonical USDai against PYUSD through the Arbitrum hub. Satellite USDai supply is tracked as bridgedSupply against the same PYUSD pool, while sUSDai separately deploys deposited USDai into GPU-backed credit strategies.

genius.notes: USD.AI publishes reserve data through its Proof of Reserves documentation and M0/Usual/Gauntlet vault disclosures, but no U.S. federal GENIUS issuer approval exists. Treat as prospective-pathway-only until a permitted payment stablecoin issuer is identified.

mintAuthority.summary: USDai uses a collateralized hub implementation on Arbitrum and uncapped OToken implementations on Ethereum, Base, and Plasma. The three satellite DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE Safes can immediately grant themselves BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE and mint without a token cap. All four transparent proxies share deterministic addresses and chain-local state; their ProxyAdmins are owned by separate 48-hour DVNTimelocks governed by 3-of-3 proposer and executor Safes.

controls.label: USDai satellite DEFAULT_ADMIN Safes

routeChecks.signingModel: The same three owners formed distinct 3-of-3 Safe instances on every reviewed chain. Ethereum and Base enabled chain-local Zodiac Delay modules with 604,800-second cooldowns; Plasma had no enabled module. All instances had zero guard and module guard.
routeChecks.rateLimits: OToken source applies no aggregate or per-call mint ceiling. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can grant BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE directly, so each current satellite Safe can bypass the bridge contract and mint arbitrary supply immediately.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Safe was DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder on each OToken satellite and owner of each immutable OBridge contract. It is separately an executor, but not the sole proposer, for the 172,800-second upgrade timelock.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526129, Base block 48592766, and Plasma block 27034527, OToken hasRole reads returned true for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the chain-local 0x5F0B...841F Safe and true for BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE on OBridge 0xffa1...bae5. The Safe owner set was 0xe982...a69C, 0x9868...79b2, and 0xD1Af...b75e with threshold 3. Ethereum enabled module 0x719f...41AB, Base enabled 0x2ab9...2803, and Plasma enabled none; the two Delay modules were owned by and targeted their respective Safes, had zero guards, and enforced 604,800-second cooldown and expiration windows.

controls.label: USDai OBridge mint contracts
controls.capDescription: Satellite mint calls are uncapped at token level but require the current OBridge caller; the Arbitrum hub implementation separately underflow-checks mint against bridgedSupply, which was 2,123,929.642271 USDai at the cutoff.

sources.label: Arbitrum exact-match USDai hub implementation source

controls.evidence: The same-address OBridge was a direct immutable deployment on all four chains: exact-block runtime lengths were nonzero and every EIP-1967 implementation, admin, and beacon slot was zero. owner() returned the local 0x5F0B...841F Safe everywhere. Ethereum, Base, and Plasma OTokens granted it BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE. Arbitrum's exact-source hub instead hard-codes it as _bridgeAdapter and decrements bridgedSupply on mint, preventing the bridge caller from creating more hub supply than was previously burned outbound.

controls.label: USDai four-chain ProxyAdmin timelocks

routeChecks.signingModel: Each chain-local timelock was self-administered. Safe 0x783b...a07b was sole proposer and canceller and one executor; Safe 0x5F0B...841F was the other executor. Both Safes had the same three owners and threshold 3.
routeChecks.rateLimits: getMinDelay() returned 172,800 seconds on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and Plasma. No RoleRevoked or MinDelayChange event occurred before the cutoff after each deployment.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: Each chain-local ProxyAdmin 0x2ddf...dc3c was owned by its local DVNTimelock. An executed operation can replace the USDai/OToken implementation and therefore remove every current mint constraint.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526129, Arbitrum block 483535601, Base block 48592766, and Plasma block 27034527, the shared-address ProxyAdmin 0x2ddf...dc3c owned each local token proxy and owner() returned the local DVNTimelock 0x0eea...639b. Each timelock returned a 172,800-second minimum delay. Complete RoleGranted/RoleRevoked histories resolved sole proposer and canceller Safe 0x783b...a07b plus executors 0x783b...a07b and 0x5F0B...841F, with no revocation before cutoff. The four exact block hashes were 0xd2eca668433c517ab710c73c244a2545203f12b35a83e4fb521595be762bdc3f, 0x45f33e882390a11b041d42014a808f848530c07e7c2d1738e8da692c4af5ca14, 0xa99a4dae34debb8307285b94373592fafc63005a817dbf45d54d48607a821872, and 0x32277619ba915b2f7d5ba0ba851ef2516efe0b99139c4df5fa67aaf0b17c62f5.

controls.label: USDai timelock proposer and canceller Safes

routeChecks.signingModel: All four chain-local Safes had owners 0xe982...a69C, 0x9868...79b2, and 0xD1Af...b75e with threshold 3. Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base each enabled one chain-local Zodiac Delay module; Plasma enabled none.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The direct Safe route can schedule and cancel upgrades immediately, but execution remains subject to the DVNTimelock's 172,800-second minimum delay.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The proposer Safe cannot bypass the timelock as ProxyAdmin owner. Its Delay module provides a slower alternate Safe execution path and does not remove the downstream 48-hour upgrade delay.

controls.evidence: Exact-block Safe reads returned the same 3-of-3 signer set on all four chains, no guard or module guard, and standard fallback handler 0xfd07...Ec99. Ethereum enabled Delay module 0xa9b6...fbc2, Arbitrum 0x0f01...96c4, and Base 0x97d9...baa4; Plasma had no module. Each Delay module was a fixed EIP-1167 clone, was owned by and targeted its local Safe, had zero guard, and used 604,800-second cooldown and expiration values.

controls.label: USDai three-chain Zodiac module controller Safe
controls.evidence: The same-address 3-of-5 Safe was the sole enabled upstream module of both Zodiac Delay paths on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base. Its chain-local instances had the listed owners, no enabled modules, zero guard and module guard, and the standard fallback handler. It can cause a satellite admin Safe to grant mint authority after the 604,800-second module cooldown, or queue upgrade scheduling through the proposer Safe before the additional 172,800-second DVNTimelock delay. It was not enabled on either Plasma Safe at the cutoff.

review.evidence: Deployment-complete review at Ethereum block 25526129, Arbitrum block 483535601, Base block 48592766, and Plasma block 27034527. The four same-address transparent proxies resolved respectively to implementations 0x3019...e5ad, 0x2af5...5bc4, 0x3019...e5ad, and 0xe306...f4cc, and all four admin slots resolved to ProxyAdmin 0x2ddf...dc3c. Satellite OTokens granted DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE to chain-local 3-of-3 Safe 0x5F0B...841F and BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE to immutable OBridge 0xffa1...bae5; the Safe can grant itself that uncapped mint role immediately. The Arbitrum hub mints only against collateral, escrowed base yield, or stored bridgedSupply under current exact-source code. Each ProxyAdmin owner was a 172,800-second DVNTimelock with exact proposer, executor, and canceller Safe identities. Chain-local Safe module inventories were reviewed through the 3-of-5 upstream Safe and 604,800-second Zodiac Delay paths; no guard or unreviewed module remained.
